claims.text: Controlled post-deposition annealing increases the effective thermal conductivity of a tungsten-based high-entropy-alloy intermediate layer.
Controlled post-deposition annealing preserves the structural integrity of the tungsten-based HEA layer.
The as-deposited tungsten-based HEA layer has a heterogeneous, coarse-grained microstructure.
Irregular grain boundaries and local inhomogeneities make the as-deposited layer's thermal conductivity suboptimal.
The proposed intervention is annealing at 900 °C for 5 hours immediately after deposition.
Temperatures of approximately 600–800 °C with cyclic thermal and mechanical loading are representative operating conditions for the proposed reactor intermediate layer.
Annealing refines the grain structure and produces a more homogeneous grain-size distribution.
Annealing promotes the formation of coherent nanoprecipitates in the tungsten-based HEA.
Coherent nanoprecipitates reduce thermal boundary resistance.
Annealing promotes atomic diffusion and chemical homogenization.
The annealed microstructure has fewer and more coherent grain boundaries.
Fewer and more coherent grain boundaries reduce phonon scattering and enhance electron and phonon transport.
Microstructural changes caused by annealing retain or improve strength and resistance to thermomechanical stress.
The annealed layer will have higher effective thermal conductivity than the untreated layer.
The annealed layer will preserve or improve strength and ductility under high-temperature cyclic loading.
The current as-deposited intermediate layer has lower heat-transfer performance and localized weaknesses under high heat flux.
Excessively high annealing temperature or duration can cause coarsening or phase instability that compromises structural integrity.
The magnitude of improvement and long-term cycling stability depend on alloy composition and annealing conditions.
The experiment compares as-deposited controls with samples annealed at 900 °C for 5 hours using thermal-conductivity, mechanical-property, and microstructural measurements.
The hypothesis is falsified if annealing produces no statistically significant conductivity increase or causes measurable mechanical deterioration under the stated loading conditions.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as coarse-grained and annealing is said to refine it, which normally implies smaller grains and more grain-boundary area, while the mechanism simultaneously attributes the benefit to having fewer grain boundaries.
